source: CAST: Character-and-Scene Episodic Memory for Agents
summary: Pairs a graph-based semantic memory index with a scene-based episodic index organised around character profiles, providing structured long-term memory for agents across sessions.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — episodic memory theme already covered by open issue HID-188; no new gap identified

source: MARS: Meta-cognitive Reflection for Efficient Self-Improvement (arXiv:2601.11974)
summary: Combines principle-based and procedural reflection into a single cycle so an agent distils rules and step-by-step strategies from errors without costly multi-turn loops. ACL 2026 long paper.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — reflects on failures and distils improvement rules, conceptually related to plan-repair (HID-186) and skill distillation, but backlog is full at 10 issues and partial-retry theme is already tracked

source: ARCANA: Reflective Multi-Agent Program Synthesis for ARC-AGI-2 (arXiv:2607.09059)
summary: Four-role multi-agent pipeline (perception, hypothesis, symbolic executor, reflective critic) coordinating via a differentiable blackboard and learned controller to solve ARC-AGI-2 under tight compute budgets.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — ARC-AGI-2 domain-specific; multi-agent blackboard/controller architecture is too far from AgentForge's sequential CLI-subprocess model

summary: Expands coding-agent evaluation beyond issue resolution to codebase Q&A, test writing, and refactoring across 284 tasks; designed as a contamination-resistant successor to SWE-bench.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — benchmark infrastructure; does not introduce an orchestration technique that AgentForge can adopt

summary: LangGraph 1.0 ships durable execution via checkpointing at each node; Temporal integration adds automatic failure recovery and days-long human-in-the-loop pauses without code rewrites.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — durable checkpoint/resume capability is thematically related to partial-retry (HID-186) and automatic retry (HID-167); no additional gap since both are already tracked

summary: Microsoft's Agent Framework reached GA in April 2026 as the successor to AutoGen; adds a built-in multi-agent graph and MCP client integration. AutoGen moves to maintenance mode.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — general framework news; AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses, not the AutoGen/MAF SDK

summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' in February 2026 to describe the shift to composing agents/skills/prompts/MCP rather than writing code directly; highlights abstraction layers (memory, permissions, tools, hooks) as the new programming surface.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — conceptual framing; no specific technique or gap to implement

source: ODYSSE: Episode-wise Policy Optimization for Agentic Reasoning (arXiv:2607.25369)
summary: RL-based approach treating agent episodes as policy-optimisation training steps to improve multi-step agentic reasoning through reward signals.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL training loop, explicitly flagged as a red-flag pattern in the research guidelines; no fit with AgentForge's deterministic CLI-subprocess model
